title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: Adults reporting a Body Mass Index over 25. People who are overweight or obese are at increased risk for heart disease and diabetes.  Neighborhood factors such as walkability and the types of food retail outlets available can impact residents' risk of being overweight or obese.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: ED visits related to bicycle injuries.  Bicycle injury ED visits can indicate the overall safety of cycling in the city.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: Transportation-related ED visits for pedestrians. Pedestrian injury ED visits can indicate the safety of walking for transportation.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: Deaths before age 65. This can indicate the overall health of a population.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: The percent of a neighborhood that is shaded by trees. Tree shade can lower a neighborhood's temperature, making it more comfortable for physical activity.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: Sidewalk area percentage. Sidewalks are important for commuting, businesses, and physical activity. More sidewalk area contributes to a safer pedestrian environment, supports vibrant business districts and can foster social interaction.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: The percentage of the population who live within walking distance to a park: a quarter-mile or less to entrances of smaller sites, such as sitting areas and playgrounds, and half-mile or less to entrances of larger parks. Increased access to green space and open space can contribute to increased levels of physical activity.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: Percent of street milage with bike lanes. Bike lanes can improve bicyclist and pedestrian safety, physical activity, and sustainable transportation use.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_name: Walking distance to a subway station
indicator_description: The percentage of population within a quarter-mile of a subway station entrance. When more people have convenient access to the transit system, they're more likely to use it. Subway access encourages active transportation, which improves the health of residents.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_name: Adults reporting mice or rats outside
indicator_description: Mice and rats are a source of household allergens connected to developing or worsening asthma.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: Households with incomes below the federal poverty level. Households without sufficient resources are often deprived of access to health care, good quality housing, and other resources that protect health.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: Adults reporting their neighborhood is safe from crime. Whether people perceive their neighborhood as safe can affect whether they will spend time outside, use parks, and use active and sustainable forms of transportation. It can also affect mental well-being.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: Adults reporting having ridden a bicycle at least once a month in the past year.

title: Active_Design_Physical_Activity_and_Health
indicator_description: Adults reporting exercise in the past 30 days (from when they were surveyed). Regular exercise is a key way to stay healthy.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_name: Adults with a recent asthma attack
indicator_description: Adults reporting an asthma diagnosis, and symptoms, in the last 12 months (from when they were surveyed). Poor air quality and housing issues increase risk of developing and triggering asthma.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Emergency department visits for asthma. Things like smoke, air pollution, dust mites, cockroaches, mold, pollen and pet dander can trigger asthma.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Hospitalizations for asthma. These more severe asthma outcomes are often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Hospitalizations for asthma. These more severe asthma outcomes are often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_name: Asthma emergency department visits due to PM2.5
indicator_description: ED visits for asthma due to PM2.5 air pollution. These represent part of the health burden of air pollution.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_name: Asthma emergency department visits due to Ozone
indicator_description: ED visits for asthma due to ozone. These are part of the health burden of air pollution.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Hospitalizations for asthma due to ozone. These are part of the health burden of air pollution.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Households reporting cracks or holes in the home. This maintenance problem is linked to mice, rats, and cockroaches - which can harm residents' health.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Households reporting leaks from outside the unit. This maintenance problem can introduce mold, which can worsen respiratory conditions like asthma.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_name: Renter-occupied homes with any health-related housing problems
indicator_description: Renter-occupied homes with any health-related housing problems. Homes with housing problems can threaten the health of the people who live there.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Adults reporting secondhand smoke at home. Secondhand smoke, especially indoors, is bad for health - particularly for the health of children.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: The presence of cockroaches in the home is often associated with poor housing maintenance. Cockroaches in the home can contaminate food and worsen asthma.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Adults without a smoke-free home policy. A smoke-free home policy can limit people's exposure to secondhand smoke, which is especially dangerous to children.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Adults reporting mold in the home. Mold can worsen respiratory conditions like asthma, and indicate housing problems in a building.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_name: Adults reporting mice or rats inside
indicator_description: Mice and rats are a source of household allergens connected to developing or worsening asthma.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Concentration of fine particles in the air. Fine particles are emitted by vehicles, building boilers, and other combustion — and are a major form of air pollution that harms health. Neighborhood sensors measure PM2.5 at the street-level, where people are most active. These sensors are designed to let us measure differences in air pollution over time and locations within New York City.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Concentration of ozone in the air. Ozone is a common air pollutant that can harm breathing and worsen respiratory conditions.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Households with incomes below the federal poverty level. Households without sufficient resources are often deprived of access to health care, good quality housing, and other resources that protect health.

title: Asthma_and_the_Environment
indicator_description: Adults with any kind of health insurance. People with health insurance are more likely to have a regular doctor, receive preventive care services, better manage chronic health conditions, and have longer life expectancy.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_name: Homes near structures rated good or excellent
indicator_description: Building quality predicts the number of housing maintenance problems in a residence that place residents at increased risk of acute or chronic health problems.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_description: Land covered by trees, grass, or other plants. Vegetative cover reduces temperatures in the immediate area, and may increase air quality.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_description: Older adults (over 65) are more vulnerable to hot weather and heat stress. Air conditioning reduces the risk of heat stroke and other heat-related illness.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_name: Residents living in a hurricane evacuation zone
indicator_description: Hurricane Evacuation Zones are determined by New York City Emergency Management and indicate varying threat levels of coastal flooding from storm surge. Evacuation orders may be given during hurricanes or coastal flooding events. There are six zones, ranked by storm surge risk. Zone 1 is the highest risk for flooding. Residents in these zones may receive evacuation orders during hurricanes or tropical storms.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_description: Spatial average of surface temperature, measured by satellite. Surface temperatures vary because of vegetative cover (which promotes cooling), and paved roads, sidewalks, and buildings (which retain heat). Hotter neighborhoods tend to have more heat-exacerbated deaths associated with extreme heat events.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_description: Emergency department visits for asthma. Things like smoke, air pollution, dust mites, cockroaches, mold, pollen and pet dander can trigger asthma.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_description: Households with incomes below the federal poverty level. Households without sufficient resources are often deprived of access to health care, good quality housing, and other resources that protect health.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_description: Mental health conditions like series psychological distress can be worsened by extreme weather such as heat waves and coastal storms.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_description: Adults reporting independent living difficulty due to a physical, mental, or emotional problem. People with disabilities may need additional support during extreme weather. For example, extra planning for safe travel out of evacuation zones during a hurricane, or back-up electricity to support medical equipment during power outages.

title: Climate_and_Health
indicator_description: People age 65+ living alone. People living alone may have more difficulty getting resources they need in an emergency, and are at higher risk of weather-related illnesses like heat stroke and hypothermia.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Hospitalizations due to heat stress. These are part of the public health burden of hot weather.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Blood lead levels above 5 mcg/dL among children under age 6. Lead poisoning can cause learning and behavior problems, and delay growth and mental development. There is no safe level of lead in the blood.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Hospitalizations for asthma. These more severe asthma outcomes are often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Hospitalizations for asthma. These more severe asthma outcomes are often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Households reporting cracks or holes in the home. This maintenance problem is linked to mice, rats, and cockroaches - which can harm residents' health.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Housing built before 1960 with peeling paint. This can put residents at risk of lead poisoning. Lead paint was banned from household paints in New York City in 1960 and in the USA in 1978.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Households reporting leaks from outside the unit. This maintenance problem can introduce mold, which can worsen respiratory conditions like asthma.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Households using supplemental heat, like a space heater. This may mean a building's main heat source doesn't work. It can indicate the presence of other health-threatening maintenance deficiencies, and increase fire risk.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Carbon monoxide incidents when there was no alarm. Carbon monoxide detectors are required in NYC homes by law. Failure to provide or maintain a detector can put people at risk for carbon monoxide poisoning and death.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Households reporting functioning air conditioning (AC). AC is an important way to prevent heat stress, especially for people with limited mobility.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_name: Renter-occupied homes with any health-related housing problems
indicator_description: Renter-occupied homes with any health-related housing problems. Homes with housing problems can threaten the health of the people who live there.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_name: Homes with mice or rats in the building
indicator_description: Households reporting mice or rats in their building in the past 90 days (from when they were surveyed). The presence of rodents is associated with housing problems. These pests can contaminate food and worsen asthma.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: The presence of cockroaches in the home is often associated with poor housing maintenance. Cockroaches in the home can contaminate food and worsen asthma.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Adults reporting mold in the home. Mold can worsen respiratory conditions like asthma, and indicate housing problems in a building.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Households with more than one person per room.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Children living in households in poverty. Poverty deprives people of access to health and safety resources.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Renter households spending 30% of their income or more on rent.

title: Housing_and_Health
indicator_description: Court-ordered evictions. Eviction often leads to residential instability, moving into poor quality housing, overcrowding, and homelessness, all of which is associated with negative health among adults and children. People who are threatened with eviction, even before they lose their home, are more likely to report poor health.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Estimated annual deaths due to PM2.5 air pollution. Estimating these deaths is a way to understand how air pollution increases mortality.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_name: Asthma emergency department visits due to PM2.5
indicator_description: ED visits for asthma due to PM2.5 air pollution. These represent part of the health burden of air pollution.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Hospitalizations for respiratory issues due to PM2.5 pollution (among people over age 20). These represent part of the health burden of air pollution.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Hospitalizations for cardiovascular issues due to PM2.5 (among people over age 40). These represent part of the health burden of air pollution.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_name: Cardiac and respiratory deaths due to Ozone
indicator_description: Deaths due to cardiac or respiratory issues linked to ozone. These show how air pollution increases mortality.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_name: Asthma emergency department visits due to Ozone
indicator_description: ED visits for asthma due to ozone. These are part of the health burden of air pollution.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Hospitalizations for asthma due to ozone. These are part of the health burden of air pollution.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Boilers are a common source of SO2, which can worsen lung disease.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Boilers are a common source of PM2.5, which can harm health.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Boilers are a common source of NOx emissions, which can harm health.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Concentration of fine particles in the air. Fine particles are emitted by vehicles, building boilers, and other combustion — and are a major form of air pollution that harms health. Neighborhood sensors measure PM2.5 at the street-level, where people are most active. These sensors are designed to let us measure differences in air pollution over time and locations within New York City.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Concentration of black carbon in the air. Black carbon is a major component of fine particles, which contribute to both short-term health effects and chronic illness

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Concentration of nitrogen dioxide in the air. Nitrogen dioxide is a pollutant formed by combustion. It causes breathing problems and contributes to smog and acid rain.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Concentration of ozone in the air. Ozone is a common air pollutant that can harm breathing and worsen respiratory conditions.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Benzene is an air pollutant resulting from motor vehicle and industrial emissions and tobacco smoke. Benzene is a known carcinogen that can also harm bone marrow and red blood cell function.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Formaldehyde is an air pollutant resulting from car exhaust and the manufacture of industrial products. Formaldehyde is a known carcinogen that can also cause irritation to eyes and lungs and increase risk of asthma and trigger asthma symptoms.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Annual vehicle miles travelled. Traffic density can influence health as a source of air pollution and traffic-related injuries.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Annual vehicle miles travelled by cars. Traffic density can influence health as a source of air pollution and traffic-related injuries.

title: Outdoor_Air_and_Health
indicator_description: Annual vehicle miles travelled by trucks. Traffic density can influence health as a source of air pollution and traffic-related injuries.
